Whether a pair's error changes across the power range

Source: R/agreement.R
level_dependence.Rd

The finding a single average difference hides, stated as a test rather than left to the eye: the extreme bands' gains, and whether their intervals are separated.

Usage

level_dependence(by_level)

Arguments

by_level

Result of agreement_by_level().

Value

A tibble with one row per source pair per run, giving the lowest and highest gain, the bands they came from, and separated.

Details

The test is on the per-cent gain, not on watts. A meter that is a constant 2.5% out reads further from its partner at 300 W than at 100 W, so a watts comparison of the extreme bands separates for every clean percentage meter. In per cent, that meter is flat and only a level-dependent one separates.

Separation is non-overlapping 95% intervals, so there is no threshold constant to argue about; a pair with too few seconds to resolve anything does not fire.

See also

Other agreement: agreement_by_level(), power_agreement()

Examples

aligned <- read_rides(demo_rides()) |> align_rides()
agreement_by_level(aligned) |> level_dependence()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   run   source_a source_b low_band  low_gain high_band high_gain separated
#>   <chr> <chr>    <chr>    <chr>        <dbl> <chr>         <dbl> <lgl>    
#> 1 run1  assioma  kickr    175–200 W     2.30 75–100 W       3.20 FALSE    
#> 2 run2  assioma  quarq    300–325 W    -5.25 50–75 W        3.71 TRUE
